scope: The original review preview separates the list of Parkinson symptoms from its botanical inventory. scope: The University of L'Aquila record authenticates the article and lists a 1.54 MB publisher PDF restricted to authorized users. The author abstract covers saffron compounds, Parkinson and depression among different contexts. The Wiley abstract and reference display leave the study-level exposure and depression comparisons open.
remaining_source_access: Use the institutional record's copy-request route or obtain an authorized copy of Phytotherapy Research 38, pp. 2482–2495. Inspect the Parkinson and depression contexts separately.

scope: The original structured abstract reports 64 directly included records from a search through April 30, 2024. The displayed references include a saffron-versus-sertraline depression trial outside Parkinson and a separate Alzheimer's trial. The author-upload listing offers a request route and the public publisher preview leaves the exact Parkinson-depression study tables unavailable.
remaining_source_access: Obtain the full Phytomedicine article 156097 and trace any explicitly matched Parkinson-depression findings to their original exposure and population.

scope: The original Tables 1–3 separate the Jin chronic-stress rat depression study from the Wang 6-OHDA Parkinson rat study. Jin measured depressive-like behavior with isolated rosmarinic acid. Wang measured striatal dopamine and dopaminergic neuron preservation. Table 3's human row concerns high-rosmarinic spearmint and knee osteoarthritis. These comparisons supply constituent and model context for fresh rosemary.
remaining_source_access: The original review prose in volume 393, pp. 1779–1795, remains gated. Retain the direct source links for the full discussion and exact underlying comparisons.

scope: The original preview lists insomnia in Parkinson background and Crocus sativus in a separate herbal inventory. The available paper segments do not isolate a ground saffron Parkinson insomnia result or confirm how the review distinguishes sleep quality and insomnia severity.
remaining_source_access: Read the full Crocus section and extract any separate insomnia scale, ingredient preparation and population from cited primary studies.

scope: The original Table III places ginger-containing foods and drinks under nausea management for dopamine agonists. scope: The original review preview names rigidity in Parkinson background. The displayed saffron fly citation concerns locomotor climbing and the identified human crocin source reports a motor total. The complete review still needs a check for a separately reported rigidity item with clinically relevant culinary exposure.
remaining_source_access: Inspect the full Crocus methods and outcomes and trace any isolated rigidity measures to their original clinical or model records.

scope: The preview lists fatigue as a symptom and saffron as a reviewed botanical in separate material. No preparation-specific Parkinson fatigue comparison is attributable from the preview, the verified references or the public author record.
remaining_source_access: Obtain the complete review and check the Crocus evidence table for a separate fatigue instrument and exposure matching dried saffron.

scope: The primary publisher and PubMed identify Part II as the Alzheimer review and Part I as the separate Parkinson review. remaining_source_access: Inspect the exact 20-page Part II deposit or authorized publisher copy, pp. 251–270, to verify the Crocus section and whether it includes any fatigue measure across diagnoses.

scope: The official Hebrew record and PubMed English abstract place cranberry under urinary infection prevention, acupuncture under depression and tai chi under Parkinson. The original Hebrew download page displays access options and supplies no public full narrative. No dried cranberry depression measure appears in either abstract.
remaining_source_access: Obtain authorized Harefuah 154(1), pp. 9–15. Read the original citation links for the three separate conditions and therapies.

scope: The original publisher sections identify dried ginger rhizome as laboratory starting material and seven isolated analytes tested in an artificial membrane permeability assay. The verified conclusion identifies three passive-permeability compounds. Animal anxiety and Parkinson studies occur in the introduction as previous work. The measured outcome is membrane diffusion in this experiment.
remaining_source_access: The Semmelweis deposit remains restricted. Obtain the full assay table, numerical permeability estimates and reproducibility details for the five-page article 112820.

scope: The original publisher introduction discusses customary tea use for tiredness. An original methods excerpt identifies the PINK1 fly experiment and the results excerpt compares fly locomotor capacity. The test compound is EGCG and the outcomes are locomotion, neuronal and metabolic readouts. This is a related constituent model with no clinical brewed tea fatigue estimate in the inspected sections.
remaining_source_access: Complete dose and outcome tables, the figures and the matching SSRN 7217951 body remain open. The journal and preprint are one evidence family.
